chunks.title: Orbital walls & apex
chunks.tldr: Orbit = 4-walled pyramid, volume ~30 mL, globe only ⅕. Roof: frontal + lesser sphenoid (optic canal, lacrimal fossa). Lateral: zygoma + greater sphenoid — strongest. Floor: maxilla — blowout fractures, infraorbital nerve. Medial: lamina papyracea (ethmoid) — paper-thin, ethmoid sinusitis spreads here. Lateral walls 90° apart; each lateral–medial 45°.
points: Superior orbital fissure (SOF): outside annulus — lacrimal, frontal, trochlear (IV) nerves + superior ophthalmic vein; inside annulus of Zinn — III (both divisions), VI, nasociliary.
Optic canal (inside annulus): optic nerve + ophthalmic artery.
Inferior orbital fissure: maxillary nerve (V2) → infraorbital nerve; route to pterygoid plexus.
All extraocular muscles arise at the apex except the inferior oblique.
Roof defects (NF1) → pulsatile globe; sphenoid sinusitis can affect the optic nerve.
chunks.hook: Lateral is tough, medial is paper, floor breaks.

cards.q: Which structures pass through the SOF inside the annulus of Zinn?
cards.a: Superior and inferior divisions of III, VI and the nasociliary nerve.

cards.q: Which extraocular muscle does not arise from the orbital apex?
cards.a: Inferior oblique (arises from the anteromedial orbital floor).

chunks.title: Blood supply & venous drainage
chunks.tldr: Ophthalmic artery = 1st branch of intracranial ICA; runs under the optic nerve through the canal. Branches: central retinal artery (1st; enters nerve 8–15 mm behind globe), lacrimal, muscular (→ anterior ciliary), short posterior ciliary (choroid + nerve head), 2 long posterior ciliary (→ major arterial circle of iris), palpebral, supraorbital/supratrochlear. Veins: superior/inferior ophthalmic → cavernous sinus (via SOF) and pterygoid plexus.
points: Valveless facial–ophthalmic venous link → periorbital skin infection can cause cavernous sinus thrombosis.
Vortex veins (4, one per posterior quadrant) drain the choroid.
Lid arcades anastomose with external carotid via the facial artery.
chunks.hook: Ophthalmic artery: first off ICA, first branch central retinal artery.

cards.q: Why can a facial skin infection cause cavernous sinus thrombosis?
cards.a: Supraorbital/angular veins drain via the superior ophthalmic vein directly into the cavernous sinus.

chunks.title: Conjunctiva, Tenon's & sclera
chunks.tldr: Conjunctiva: palpebral (stuck to tarsus) → fornix → bulbar (loose). Epithelium 2–5 layers columnar + goblet cells (mucin). Stroma: adenoid layer appears only after 2–3 months → neonatal conjunctivitis is papillary, not follicular. Accessory lacrimal glands: Krause (fornices), Wolfring (upper tarsal border). Tenon's capsule: limbus → optic nerve; check ligaments; Lockwood's ligament supports globe. Sclera: collagen, 0.3 mm under recti, 0.6 mm elsewhere; opaque because irregular lamellae + more water.
points: Conjunctiva sensation: V1; few pain fibres.
Conjunctiva + Tenon's + episclera fused at limbus for ~3 mm.
Long posterior ciliary arteries/nerves run at 3 and 9 o'clock.
Anterior ciliary vessels enter ~4 mm behind limbus; vortex veins exit just behind equator.
Lamina cribrosa: scleral collagen bands at the optic nerve exit.
chunks.hook: Babies have no adenoid layer → no follicles under 3 months.

cards.q: Why is neonatal inclusion conjunctivitis papillary rather than follicular?
cards.a: The conjunctival adenoid (lymphoid) layer doesn't develop until 2–3 months of age.

chunks.title: Cornea
chunks.tldr: ~550 µm centrally, 11.7 × 10.6 mm. Five layers: epithelium (5–6 cells), Bowman (acellular), stroma (90%, regular collagen lamellae), Descemet (endothelial basement membrane, 3 µm at birth → 10–12 µm adult), endothelium (single layer, pumps → deturgescence). Endothelial density ~3500 (birth) → ~2000 cells/mm² (old age); repair only by cell enlargement/sliding. Clarity = uniform structure + avascularity + deturgescence.
points: Nutrition: limbal vessels, aqueous, tears; O₂ mainly from air.
Sensation: V1 via long ciliary nerves.
Endothelial failure → corneal oedema.
chunks.hook: Every Busy Student Drinks Espresso: Epithelium, Bowman, Stroma, Descemet, Endothelium.

cards.q: Three reasons the cornea is transparent?
cards.a: Uniform regular stromal structure, avascularity, deturgescence (endothelial pump).

chunks.title: Uveal tract, lens & aqueous
chunks.tldr: Iris: no anterior epithelium; sphincter/dilator from anterior epithelium; heavily pigmented posterior epithelium; capillaries non-fenestrated (no fluorescein leak). Ciliary body ~6 mm: pars plicata 2 mm (processes make aqueous; fenestrated) + pars plana 4 mm. Ciliary muscle: circular fibres → accommodation; longitudinal → open trabecular meshwork. Choroid: 3 vessel layers, choriocapillaris innermost, Bruch membrane inside. Lens: 4 × 9 mm, avascular, 65% water, 35% protein (highest in body), Y sutures (upright anterior, inverted posterior), grows lifelong.
points: Ciliary epithelium: inner non-pigmented (from neuroretina), outer pigmented (from RPE).
Lens: no nerves, vessels or pain fibres; potassium, ascorbate, glutathione concentrated.
Aqueous: ciliary body → posterior chamber → pupil → AC → angle.
chunks.hook: Plicata makes aqueous; plana is where we inject.

cards.q: Why do iris capillaries not leak fluorescein but ciliary process capillaries do?
cards.a: Iris capillaries are non-fenestrated; ciliary process capillaries are fenestrated.

chunks.title: Angle, retina & vitreous
chunks.tldr: Angle: Schwalbe line (end of Descemet/endothelium) → trabecular meshwork (uveal → corneoscleral, pores shrink toward Schlemm) → scleral spur. Schlemm drains via ~30 collector channels + aqueous veins to episcleral veins. Retina: 10 layers, ILM → RPE. Thickness 0.1 mm (ora) to 0.56 mm. Macula 5.5–6 mm; fovea 1.5 mm; foveola 0.3 mm, cones only, = FAZ, 4 mm temporal to disc. Blood: choriocapillaris → outer ⅓; central retinal artery → inner ⅔. Vitreous 99% water (collagen + hyaluronan); base firmly attached at pars plana/ora lifelong.
points: Retina firmly attached only at disc and ora → limits RD spread; choroidal detachments extend past the ora.
Inner blood–retinal barrier = retinal capillary endothelium; outer = RPE.
Foveola fed only by choriocapillaris → damaged irreversibly when detached.
Ora: 6.5 mm (temporal) / 5.7 mm (nasal) behind Schwalbe.

head: Retinal layer (inner → outer)
rows: ILM, nerve fibre layer, ganglion cells
Inner plexiform, inner nuclear (bipolar, amacrine, horizontal)

chunks.hook: Choroid feeds the outer third; central retinal artery the inner two-thirds.

cards.q: Where is the retina firmly attached to the RPE?
cards.a: At the optic disc and the ora serrata.

cards.q: Which part of the retina contains only cones?

chunks.title: Extraocular muscles & surgical landmarks
chunks.tldr: Recti arise from annulus of Zinn; insertions from limbus: MR 5.5, IR 6.5, LR 7.0, SR 7.7 mm (spiral of Tillaux). Vertical recti 23° to optic axis; obliques 51–54°. SO: longest/thinnest; through trochlea, inserts under SR. IO: from medial orbital floor, inserts over macula. Nerves: LR6 SO4, rest 3. Pars plana injections: 3.5–4 mm (phakic), 3–3.5 mm (pseudophakic). Pars plicata (cyclodestruction target) 2–3 mm behind limbus.
points: Ora externally: 5.5 mm nasal, 7 mm temporal (≈ rectus insertions).
Check ligaments = functional origins (pulley hypothesis).
LR also fed by lacrimal artery; IO by infraorbital artery.

cards.q: Distance behind the limbus for an intravitreal injection in a phakic eye?

chunks.title: Lids: layers, margin & retractors
chunks.tldr: Lid layers: skin (thin, no fat), orbicularis (VII; pretarsal/preseptal/orbital), areolar tissue, tarsal plate, palpebral conjunctiva. Grey line splits anterior lamella (skin + orbicularis) from posterior (tarsus + conjunctiva). Margin glands: Zeis (sebaceous, lash follicles), Moll (sweat), meibomian (posterior margin). Orbital septum: barrier lid ↔ orbit. Upper retractor: levator (III) aponeurosis → skin crease + Müller's (sympathetic). Lower: capsulopalpebral fascia from IR.
points: Ptosis occurs in both Horner (Müller) and III palsy (levator).
Whitnall's ligament: check band of levator.
Sensation: V1 (lacrimal, supraorbital, supratrochlear, infratrochlear) + V2 (infraorbital).
Lymph: lateral → preauricular/parotid; medial → submandibular.
Epicanthus normal in infants; persists in Asians.
chunks.hook: Grey line = the zip between front and back lamella.

cards.q: Why does Horner syndrome cause ptosis?
cards.a: Loss of sympathetic supply to Müller's (superior tarsal) muscle.

chunks.title: Lacrimal apparatus
chunks.tldr: Lacrimal gland: orbital lobe (in fossa) + palpebral lobe, split by levator lateral horn; ~10 ducts open in superotemporal fornix — removing the palpebral lobe cuts all ducts. Drainage: puncta → canaliculi → sac (lacrimal fossa) → nasolacrimal duct → inferior meatus. Pump: capillarity, gravity, blinking, Horner's muscle. Nerves: lacrimal (sensory V1), greater petrosal (parasympathetic secretomotor, VII → pterygopalatine ganglion), sympathetics (Vidian nerve).
points: Sac below the medial palpebral ligament is weakly covered → dacryocystitis swells/fistulates here.
Angular vessels 8 mm nasal to inner canthus → incise 2–3 mm nasal to canthus in sac surgery.
Gland lymph → preauricular nodes.
chunks.hook: Cut the palpebral lobe, dry the whole gland.

cards.q: Which nerve carries parasympathetic secretomotor fibres to the lacrimal gland?
cards.a: Greater petrosal nerve (VII) → nerve of pterygoid canal → pterygopalatine ganglion.

chunks.title: Optic nerve, chiasm & visual pathway
chunks.tldr: Optic nerve: ~1 million axons; exits 3 mm nasal to posterior pole; myelinated after lamina (1.5 → 3 mm wide). Segments: intraocular 1 mm, intraorbital 25–30 mm (S-shaped slack), intracanalicular 4–9 mm, intracranial 10 mm. Sheaths = meninges; raised ICP distends subarachnoid space. Blood: disc surface from retinal arterioles, laminar region from short posterior ciliary arteries, rest pial. Chiasm: nasal fibres cross. Tract → LGN → radiation; Meyer's loop (temporal) = superior quadrantanopia. V1 calcarine; V4 colour, V5 motion.
points: 80% visual fibres, 20% pupillary (bypass LGN → pretectum).
Ganglion cell axons are CNS → don't regenerate.
Macula represented at the occipital pole.
chunks.hook: Meyer's loop: temporal lobe lesion → pie in the sky.

cards.q: Arterial supply of the laminar optic nerve head?

chunks.title: Cranial nerves III–VII around the eye
chunks.tldr: III: between cerebral peduncles, near PComm, lateral wall of cavernous sinus → superior (SR, levator) and inferior divisions (MR, IR, IO + parasympathetic to ciliary ganglion). IV: thinnest, only dorsal exit, crosses; tentorium injury. V1: lacrimal, frontal, nasociliary (sensory nerve of the eye; tip of nose → Hutchinson sign). V2: infraorbital, damaged in floor fractures. VI: longest intracranial course, runs inside the cavernous sinus. VII: orbicularis + greater petrosal (tears).
points: All other cavernous sinus nerves run in the lateral wall; VI is free in the sinus.
Herpes zoster vesicles on the nose tip predict ocular involvement (nasociliary).
chunks.hook: VI travels furthest and sits inside the sinus — first to suffer.

cards.q: Why does a nose-tip zoster rash predict eye involvement?
cards.a: Both are supplied by the nasociliary branch of V1 (Hutchinson sign).

chunks.title: Embryology & postnatal growth
chunks.tldr: Surface ectoderm: lens, lacrimal gland, corneal/conjunctival epithelium, lid epidermis. Neural crest: keratocytes, corneal endothelium, trabecular meshwork, iris/choroid stroma, ciliary muscle, sclera, meninges. Neural ectoderm: retina, RPE, ciliary epithelium, iris sphincter/dilator, optic nerve. Mesoderm: EOMs, vascular endothelium. Timeline: optic vesicle 4 wk → cup + lens vesicle 5–6 wk → fissure closes (coloboma if not) → lids fuse 8 wk, open 5th month → hyaloid gone by 8 mo → macula mature 6 mo after birth; myelination complete 3 mo.
points: Vitreous: primary (3–6 wk, hyaloid), secondary (6–10 wk), tertiary (zonule, from 10 wk).
Nasolacrimal cord canalises just before birth (→ congenital NLDO).
Newborn eye ~16.6 mm, adult size by 7–8 yr; cornea adult size by 2 yr.
Infant irides look blue: little stromal pigment.
chunks.hook: Iris muscles are neural (not muscle) tissue; angle and endothelium are neural crest.
